references.text: The continuation of the journey by the Arnon River, which mentions the books of the Lord's wars and describes the fords of the Arnon at the border of Moab.
Balak meets Balaam at the Arnon, at the border of the land, confirming the significance of the Arnon as a boundary river.
The Lord commands Israel to cross the Arnon Valley and take the land from the Amorite king Sihon, confirming the Arnon as the border between Moab and the Amorites.
Describes Aroer on the bank of the Arnon River as part of the land Israel took from Sihon.
Describes the land taken from the two Amorite kings, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
The land from Aroer by the Arnon Valley was given to Reuben and Gad.
Describes the territory from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon River.
Sihon's kingdom extended from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon River, confirming the Arnon as a boundary.
The inheritance of Reuben extended from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon River.
Jephthah describes how Israel camped on the other side of the Arnon without crossing Moab's border.
Israel took possession of all the Amorite land from the Arnon to the Jabbok.
Prophecy concerning the daughters of Moab at the fords over the Arnon.
Prophecy against Moab mentioning the Arnon in connection with Moab's fall.
